# Known load-dependent flakes (#2397)
#
# Each non-comment line is one ExUnit failure exactly as the runner prints it:
#   <Module> :: <test name>
#
# A red CI run's failing tests are compared against this list. A test on the
# list is reported as a KNOWN FLAKE (an existing investigation owns it); a test
# not on the list is reported as a NEW FAILURE and must be treated as a real
# regression from the change. That distinction is what keeps "CI is red"
# informative: red caused only by known flakes is a flake that fired, not proof
# the change is broken.
#
# Provenance: each entry records where it was last observed (run URL or commit,
# date) so stale entries can be audited and pruned once a flake stops firing.
# Add a new entry when a flake is confirmed, using the exact name printed by the
# runner. Keep entries byte-exact — the comparison is a full-line match.
#
# Remove an entry as soon as its cause is fixed and the fix is on main or in the
# same change — do NOT keep a fixed test listed "in case it recurs". A listed
# test is reported as a known flake instead of a NEW failure, so a fixed test
# left on the list converts the very regression it would have caught back into
# noise. That is the exact signal loss this file exists to prevent, and a
# recurrence after a fix is a regression, which is precisely what must be loud.
#
# Scope: the classifier parses ExUnit's `N) test <name> (<Module>)` lines and
# runs only on the Elixir coverage partitions. Failures from other runners
# (e.g. the streamdeck Vitest job) can never match a line here, so listing them
# would be inert — track those on their own ticket instead.

# The shared-WorkflowStore-stale-config family — two Aiur.GitHub.IssuesTest
# entries and three Aiur.GitHub.BotIdentityTest entries — was listed here and is
# now removed. #2509 fixed the cause: WorkflowStore read the config twice per
# reload, once for the workflow and once for the freshness stamp, so a write
# landing between the two recorded the new content's digest against the old
# content's workflow and served the pre-write config indefinitely.
#
# Worth recording, because it is the argument for auditing the rest of this
# file: the first entry named that cause — "the shared WorkflowStore singleton,
# which can serve a stale valid config under load" — on 2026-08-23, and it was
# fixed on 2026-09-03. For eleven days five tests reported a real config-reload
# defect and were classified as noise. The entry was written honestly and the
# call was reasonable at the time; the lesson is about how long a correct
# diagnosis can sit behind a flake label, not about who wrote it.
#
# Four of the five were verified against #2509 rather than assumed: each passes
# under a companion process force-reloading the store continuously, and each
# fails again under that same pressure when #2509's single read is reverted to a
# double read (4/5, 2/5, 5/5 and 3/5 of five runs). A recurrence is now a
# regression and must report as NEW.
#
# The fifth, "normalize_issue/4 does not use the current checkout when
# repository configuration is absent", needs no such check: #2520 renamed it to
# "uses the current checkout ..." when it inverted that behaviour, so the line
# had already stopped matching anything the runner can print. Entries do not
# announce when they go inert — the match is byte-exact and a stale line looks
# exactly like a quiet one — which is a second reason to re-read this file on a
# schedule rather than only when a flake is fixed.

# decision_store_test.exs:2624 saturation dispatch ordering (#2402).
# Last observed 2026-08-23.
Aiur.DecisionStoreTest :: saturation fails admission durably and opens delivery attention

Aiur.BuildOrder.TicketHistoryProviderTest :: publishes immutable per-ticket updates and tolerates subscriber churn

# The shared PubSub/ReadCache collapse cluster (six failures in one partition at
# commit 5c1679f7, 2026-08-23) was listed here and is now removed: this change
# fixes it with the shared-children recovery, so a recurrence is a regression
# and must report as NEW.

# failure in coverage (3/4). The exact name is pinned to the test definition so
# the reporter keeps its full-line matching contract.
Aiur.GitHub.CodeOwnersTest :: user tokens become allowlist entries

# assertion is on a real shelled-out `mise`/Mix build under a build-gate lease
